items.name: grid1
items.prompt:
Create ONE image that is a clean 2x2 grid of FOUR separate, equal-sized vertical 9:16 photographs separated by thin plain white gutters, read left-to-right, top-to-bottom. Each panel is a DIFFERENT scene and camera angle as described below. Shared look for all panels: a handcrafted TABLETOP miniature diorama shot like toy / scale-model photography: the whole world is a small hand-made set built on a wooden worktable or inside an open cardboard or wooden display box, lit by a warm desk lamp; strong tilt-shift with shallow depth of field and a slightly high camera looking down onto the set; every prop and the seabed are cute, chunky and visibly hand-made (felt, cotton-wool marine snow hanging on fine threads, crumpled blue cellophane water, painted cardboard backdrops with visible seams, paper-cut rocks and kelp, clay with fingerprints, bent wire, tiny LED fairy-light bulbs for any glow); muted warm palette. the creature is the ONLY precise object: an accurately sculpted, hand-painted collectible figurine with satin paint and faint brush texture, with exactly the real anatomy, proportions and colours. It must match the attached replica (creature card) and real reference photo exactly and be identical in every panel: The body is bulbous, loose, and highly flexible, tapering to a small rear tail fin. The skin has a velvety texture covered in fine spines, colored orange-red with bright greenish-yellow mottling. It features a large mouth with a protruding lower jaw. Two small eyes with deep rosy red irises are positioned high on the head. Between the eyes sits a modified dorsal spine acting as a lure with filament bundles. It has two leg-like pectoral fins extending laterally and smaller pelvic fins underneath used for resting on the seafloor. Must not have smooth scales, a streamlined body, large bulging eyes, or standard thin swimming fins. STYLE REFERENCES: the LAST 2 attached images come from another episode of the same series — copy ONLY their hand-made tabletop-diorama look (set building, materials, desk-lamp light, tilt-shift, camera height); never copy their animal, map or objects literally. Clay figurines, boats and vehicles never make the creature look giant. Keep the upper quarter of every panel calm and uncluttered. NEVER draw text, letters, numbers, labels, arrows, logos, watermarks. Painted clay figurines are allowed; never real human hands or people. Every animal is drawn as what it REALLY is — a nickname like 'sea pig' (a sea cucumber) never means a pig; never draw land animals.
Panel 1 (top-left, wide shot): Wide shot looking down at a handcrafted miniature seabed. Crumpled blue cellophane forms the water, with paper-cut rocks scattered around. The bulbous, orange-red deep-sea anglerfish with greenish-yellow mottling rests calmly on the bottom, propped up on its leg-like pectoral and pelvic fins. The creature occupies about one-third of the frame, large enough for phone viewing, caught in the act of resting. Warm desk lamp lighting casts soft shadows. The upper quarter is calm and uncluttered. Hand-made props: crumpled blue cellophane, paper-cut rocks.
Panel 2 (top-right, medium shot): Medium shot of the creature nestled among painted clay coral rubble and suspended cotton-wool marine snow hanging on fine threads. The creature's large mouth and protruding lower jaw are visible as it waves its modified dorsal spine lure, which features tiny filament bundles made of fine wire. The camera focuses on the creature's ambush behavior. The upper quarter of the frame remains calm and uncluttered. Hand-made props: painted clay coral rubble, cotton-wool marine snow.
Panel 3 (bottom-left, wide shot): Wide shot of a cross-section cardboard display box sitting on a wooden desk edge. Inside the box, a miniature painted clay ROV shines a tiny LED fairy-light beam onto the anglerfish resting on the deep-sea floor. The box has visible seams, showing a deep-sea diorama. The upper quarter is empty black cardboard for captions. Hand-made props: cross-section cardboard box, clay ROV, wooden desk edge.
Panel 4 (bottom-right, close shot): Close shot panning across the creature's head and wrinkled, loose skin. The edge of a wooden worktable is visible. A painted clay scientist figurine holds a handcrafted wooden measuring stick next to the creature, which is accurately scaled to its 30.5cm true size (appearing small relative to the human figure). The creature's deep rosy red irises are clearly visible. Hand-made props: clay scientist figurine, wooden measuring stick.

Panel 1 (top-left, close shot): Close shot focusing on the creature's back. A miniature hand-made wire magnifying glass is propped up on a green cutting mat at the edge of the set, framing a section of the creature's skin. Through the glass, the satin paint and faint brush texture beautifully simulate the fine spines and velvety surface of the bright greenish-yellow mottled skin. Hand-made props: wire magnifying glass, green cutting mat.
Panel 2 (top-right, wide shot): Wide shot with a striking, dynamic composition. A menacing shadow from a cardboard predator claw falls across the set. The creature reacts dramatically, standing tall on its small pelvic fins like legs and inflating its bulbous body like a balloon. Hand-cut felt kelp sways around it under dramatic, warm desk lamp lighting. Hand-made props: cardboard predator claw shadow, hand-cut felt kelp.
Panel 3 (bottom-left, wide shot): Wide shot showing the edge of the wooden worktable. On the table sits a diorama of the ocean surface made of layered paper waves. A large, chunky painted clay research ship uses a miniature string net to hoist the correctly-scaled small creature out of the water. The creature remains perfectly intact and robust in the net, demonstrating its resilience. Hand-made props: paper waves, clay research ship, miniature string net.
Panel 4 (bottom-right, wide shot): Wide shot of the creature back on the dark seabed, viewed from slightly behind as it sits patiently on its fins. The set is built against a black cardboard backdrop with visible seams, and the tiny LED fairy lights scattered around the felt rocks are dimming. The creature is receding into the deep darkness as the warm lighting fades to black. Hand-made props: black cardboard backdrop, tiny LED fairy lights.
